His arrest in 2023 triggered widespread protests, including attacks on military installations, and his supporters continue to demand his release.
Article Summary: Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she says. Khan was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated.

Article Title: Imran Khan's kin say Pak govt violated court order for not taking ex-PM to private hospital
Article Text:
Imran Khan shifted back to jail after medical examination

Family alleges violation of court order

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examination amid a legal battle over his health and demands from his family and supporters for better medical care.Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said, news agaency PTI reports. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am.The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital following a medical report that said he was suffering from “level three plus” anxiety.Khan's family has repeatedly raised concerns about his access to adequate medical treatment while in custody. His sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the medical examination at PIMS, according to AP. They have accused authorities of violating a court order by taking him to a government hospital for a medical examination instead of a private hospital designated by the court.She alleged that during their meeting, Khan complained of being kept in solitary confinement, which she described as “mental torture” for the former prime minister.Khan’s personal physician, Faisal Sultan, said he had been taken to Shifa International Hospital, where he waited for Khan until early Friday. He was later informed that Khan had instead been returned to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi.Tarar said authorities changed the plan because of security concerns after supporters of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) gathered outside Shifa International Hospital or were heading there.Khan has been in custody since his arrest on August 5, 2023, in a corruption case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am. The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital.

Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s transfer follows months of health concerns, including a dispute over worsening vision in his right eye

Imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was shifted from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination, news agency AP reported citing Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party's statement.Khan was taken to Shifa International Hospital hours after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government would comply with a Supreme Court order directing authorities to facilitate his medical examination.The PTI said the transfer was carried out following the Supreme Court's order earlier this week but did not provide further details. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there.Earlier Thursday, Chaudhry said the government had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification on whether the medical relief granted to Khan applied only to him or could also cover other prisoners. He stressed that the request was not aimed at delaying or defying the court's order.The three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board examine him, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan.The government has maintained that prisoners receive medical care under existing rules and can be moved to government hospitals when required.Concerns over Khan's health intensified in January after his family claimed he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye. The government disputed the claim and later said his vision had improved by around 70%.Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. He has remained imprisoned since 2023 after convictions in multiple cases, including a graft case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was moved from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there. Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no- confidence vote in April 2022.

Article Title: Red-faced Pakistan summons top diplomat over US envoy Gor's J&K remark in Srinagar
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

Pakistan on Wednesday summoned the top US diplomat Islamabad and lodged a protest after US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India” during his visit to Srinagar on Wednesday.The remarks came as Gor made his first visit to Jammu and Kashmir since taking office and met chief minister Omar Abdullah.Gor’s comments were made during a joint media briefing with Abdullah following their meeting at the chief minister’s residence. “It’s a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here,” the US envoy said.Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, saying the US regularly reviews its warnings. He said the Indian government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration had taken steps to improve safety in the region.“I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” Gor said, adding that the US would consider whether its existing travel warning should be downgraded.The ambassador also described his meeting with Abdullah as “very good” and said the two sides had discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and create opportunities benefiting India and the US.Abdullah said the talks focused on what Washington could do for Jammu and Kashmir, while also referring to “certain legacy issues” that would need to be addressed.“We look forward to taking this conversation further,” Abdullah said, adding that he was “very hopeful and optimistic” that engagement between the US and Jammu and Kashmir would “both widen and deepen in the years ahead”.
Article Summary: Pakistan summons top US diplomat Islamabad and lodges a protest. US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India’ Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for J&K.

Article Title: Pakistan govt to challenge SC order to move jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to hospital
Article Text:
'Not within four walls of law': Pak law minister on Khan hospitalisation order

The Shehbaz Sharif-led Pakistan government will challenge the Supreme Court's order directing the transfer of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital, as law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirmed in a video message on Wednesday.According to news agency Reuters, the Pakitan Supreme Court had ordered the government to move Khan to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital within two days and allow him access to his personal physician.“This order is not within four walls of the law,” Tarar said in a video statement.He said authorities had reviewed the ruling and decided to approach the court seeking a review. “A convicted prisoner has to be treated either inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law,” Tarar said, adding that the review petition would seek a modification of the order.The move could end hopes of Imran Khan’s family and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), which have repeatedly sought better healthcare and visitation rights for the former PM.It could also trigger public discontent over his treatment in custody.Recently, Imran Khan supporters staged widespread protest over his imprisonment against Islamabad government.Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he says are politically motivated.He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment under army chief Asim Munir's influence.The Supreme Court order came after former president Arif Alvi raised concerns over World Cup winning captain and former PM's medical condition.Alvi also shared Khan's vitals on X.Imran Khan's sons have also repeatedly expressed concern about his deteriorating health, while his lawyers have claimed he suffered significant vision loss in his right eye while in prison.
Article Summary: Pakistani law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirms government will challenge the Supreme Court's order. Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment.

Article Title: Imran Khan’s sister meets him after 9 months as Pakistan SC orders hospital transfer for jailed ex-PM
Article Text:
Former Pak PM is set to be shifted to a hospital after top court's order over health concerns

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan ’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months, following a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.The meeting lasted around 15 minutes, according to jail sources, cited by Express Tribune. Noreen briefed Imran on the Supreme Court’s order regarding his transfer to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital and enquired about his health. The two also discussed ongoing legal matters.Noreen confirmed after the meeting that she had met her brother but did not speak to the media, in line with an assurance given before the court. She later left Adiala Jail with her sisters Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan.Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, with their meeting lasting around 30-35 minutes. Bushra earlier met her daughter, Mubashra Sheikh, and sister-in-law Mehrunnisa.Before entering the jail, Noreen told reporters that she would inform Imran that “the Supreme Court has granted you permission” to meet his family. She also said she would brief him about efforts made by PTI workers on his behalf.The meetings followed a three-member Supreme Court bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed directing the government to facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family. The court was hearing petitions concerning his access to his sisters and personal physicians, as well as his medical condition.The order came after a medical board report and a report by the Adiala Jail superintendent were submitted to the court. The reports recommended more frequent meetings with Imran’s immediate family and spouse to help manage his blood pressure and anxiety.The Supreme Court also ordered that Imran be moved to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the formation of a medical board comprising an eye specialist, general physician, cardiologist and his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. Dr Uzma was also to be included in the board.The court ordered that his medical records remain confidential and barred political activity or media interactions outside the hospital. It also directed authorities to arrange telephone contact between Imran and his children.Justice Waheed stressed that access to family could not be treated as a favour, describing the meetings as a fundamental right rather than a concession. The court, however, required PTI representatives to refrain from political activity or media engagement after meeting Imran, a condition the party said it would follow.Aleema Khan welcomed the order, saying the family had been demanding hospital treatment for Imran for months. Speaking to reporters at the Dahgal checkpoint in Rawalpindi, she said she was happy about the meeting but remained uncertain about whether the development signalled a broader change in circumstances.“"Words cannot describe how happy I am about the meeting. I cannot even imagine where I would have got sweets from. I have appeared before the ATC Rawalpindi from the Supreme Court,” Aleema said.She also rejected suggestions that the family was politicising Imran’s health, saying they were speaking as his sisters.PTI spokesperson Niazullah Khan Niazi said Imran had a right to meet his family twice a week but that authorities had continued to restrict access despite an Islamabad High Court order. He said the party would comply with the Supreme Court’s direction against political statements after meetings.Concerns over Imran’s health have intensified in recent months. A medical report submitted to the Supreme Court said he had experienced fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and significant anxiety.A PIMS cardiologist who examined him on August 1 recorded his blood pressure at 140/100mmHg and recommended measures to reduce mental stress, including more frequent meetings with his wife and access to reading material. A four-member medical board that examined him on August 10 recorded his blood pressure at 140/80mmHg and recommended walking, relaxation and more frequent interaction with his immediate family and spouse.The report said Imran had undergone at least 39 medical check-ups since his incarceration, with jail medical officers examining him three times a day. It also said his ECG was normal and his vision had improved to almost normal following treatment for an eye condition.PTI has questioned the authenticity and completeness of the medical documentation and demanded examinations by Imran’s personal physicians, Dr Asim Yusuf and Dr Faisal Sultan, as well as an independent medical board. The government has rejected claims that he is being denied proper medical care, saying he is receiving treatment from specialists in accordance with the law and court orders.A report submitted to the Supreme Court in February had said Imran’s right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. The court subsequently ordered that he be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. They were sentenced in December 2025 to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case over allegations that they unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince.Imran has been in custody since August 2023, initially following his conviction in the £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under Pakistan’s Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with the May 9, 2023, protests.Imran, who served as prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022, and his supporters have consistently maintained that the cases against him are politically motivated and aimed at preventing his political comeback.
Article Summary: Imran's sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months. Meeting followed a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.
